actual_mathematical_premises: All input coordinates are independent real random variables with probability densities bounded by one.
The target matrix is real symmetric and the full target assumes at least three eigenvalues of absolute value at least one.
Named partner account03/B05 supplies a delocalized spectral-projection theorem under max_j ||Pe_j||_2 <= 1/2.
account03/B01 supplies the common L3 envelope for the product of two arbitrary independent density-bounded variables.
The previous B05 cube example refutes dimension-free spectral-plane fiberwise supremum bounds.

new_results: Coarea-to-half-Riesz transfer for Q=a(X+m(Y))^2+R(Y) without assuming independence of the shifted square and R.
For probability densities g in L3, sup_t int |t-s|^{-1/2}g(s)ds <= 2^(5/2)||g||_3^(3/4).
If a 3x3 selected block has ab-d^2=ac-e^2=0, then ||p_Q||_infinity <15.842/sqrt(|a kappa|), kappa=f-de/a, uniformly over arbitrary outside couplings.
If that selected block has all three eigenvalues of absolute value at least one, then |a kappa|>=1/3 and the subclass density cap is <27.44.

The matrix [[1,1,1],[1,1,-1],[1,-1,1]] has eigenvalues 2,2,-1 but all 2x2 principal minors zero, refuting the stronger principal-pair shortcut; the new theorem still bounds its output density by <11.21.
